GO Biological Process 2023 with the default Enrichr background. BH adjustment was verified across all 1,541 returned terms before the overlap filter. The target sets contain 165 Parkinson’s, 60 vascular-dementia and 44 frontotemporal-dementia genes. tables.scope: The 27-gene shared set and the full 165-gene Parkinson’s set are tested separately.
notes: Adjusted P values are the Enrichr within-library multiple-testing results. BH denotes the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. Overlap is the number of input genes annotated to a term; term size is the number of genes annotated to that term in the library. Gene symbols are separated by semicolons.
Both analyses use GO Biological Process 2023. The shared-set table retains 185 terms with overlap ≥ 2, including 151 with adjusted P < 0.05; the top 20 are displayed in Figure 3B.

All 2,021 returned terms are included for the Parkinson’s set; 472 meet adjusted P < 0.05 and overlap ≥ 2. Enrichr accepted 165 genes, of which 151 have annotations. BH adjustment is across returned terms; the sensitivity includes all 5,407 library terms. The default Enrichr background was used, not a graph-matched background.

The full Parkinson’s enrichment results include mitochondrial autophagy, fission and membrane-potential terms. These PD terms are not displayed in the retained Figure 3B, which shows only the shared 27-gene analysis. Shared-27 overlap columns refer to the shared input set. Enrichment is not a test of specificity to menopause.

tables.name: S13_Symptom_PageRank
tables.title: Dementia-seeded PageRank of perimenopausal symptoms
tables.scope: Rankings for all 1,891 symptoms and a summary of the seven selected perimenopausal symptoms.
notes: Personalized PageRank measures graph proximity to the specified seed. Ranks and percentiles are descriptive. Membership in a ranked gene set does not require a direct gene–disease association.
Dementia is the PageRank seed (DOID:1307); damping 0.85, maximum 500 iterations and tolerance 1e-20. Rank/N is a descriptive rank fraction, not a null-test P value.
Direct-route queries here cover insomnia and paresthesia. Blank route counts identify symptoms not queried directly; they do not establish an absence of routes.

tables.name: S16_Bone_brain_genes
tables.title: Genes shared by the osteoporosis and dementia PageRank rankings
tables.scope: Fourteen genes shared by the top-200 condition-specific lists; eight also belong to the premature-menopause top 200.
notes: Personalized PageRank measures graph proximity to the specified seed. Ranks and percentiles are descriptive. Membership in a ranked gene set does not require a direct gene–disease association.

Rankings use the 19,507-gene identifier universe of the DWPC graph and scores from the human-focused graph. The gene overlap and its enrichment are separate from the osteoporosis–dementia DWPC analysis.

tables.name: S17_Bone_brain_enrichment
tables.title: Enrichment of the 14 osteoporosis–dementia overlap genes
tables.scope: The 1,284 significant terms retained from the five-library enrichment.
notes: Adjusted P values are the Enrichr within-library multiple-testing results. BH denotes the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. Overlap is the number of input genes annotated to a term; term size is the number of genes annotated to that term in the library. Gene symbols are separated by semicolons.

Libraries: GO Biological Process 2023, KEGG 2021 Human, Reactome 2022, WikiPathway 2023 Human and Jensen DISEASES. Adjustments are separate within each library; the libraries are not independent replications.
Only terms with adjusted P < 0.05 are present in this analysis export. Figure 5B shows DWPC schemas and was not generated from this 14-gene enrichment.

tables.name: S21_APO_shared_genes
tables.title: Ranked genes shared by adverse pregnancy outcomes, menopause symptoms and cognition
tables.scope: All selected genes from the three top-2% PageRank sets, with shared membership identified.
notes: Personalized PageRank measures graph proximity to the specified seed. Ranks and percentiles are descriptive. Membership in a ranked gene set does not require a direct gene–disease association.

Uniform multiseed PageRank uses damping 0.85, tolerance 1e-10 and 500 maximum iterations. Candidate genes lie within two breadth-first-search hops of the group seeds. The top 2% is rounded up within each connected candidate set.
The selected sets contain 374, 276 and 372 genes, respectively. A gene may have one record per group. Membership counts identify pairwise and three-way overlaps; 36 genes occur in all three groups.

tables.name: S22_APO_overlap_statistics
tables.title: Overlap statistics and sensitivity for the adverse-pregnancy-outcome, menopause and cognition gene sets
tables.scope: Set sizes, Jaccard similarities, Fisher tests, degree-matched null comparisons and threshold sensitivity.
notes: APO, adverse pregnancy outcome. Jaccard similarity is intersection divided by union. Pairwise counts include genes present in all three sets.
Fisher tests use the 20,473-gene universe implicit in their contingency counts. A stored P value of zero reflects numerical underflow, not an exactly zero probability.

The degree-matched null uses 1,000 permutations, 20 log1p-degree bins, an 18,753-connected-gene universe and random seed 42. Empirical P values use a plus-one correction. This comparison uses a different universe from the Fisher tests.
Top-percent thresholds in the sensitivity table are expressed as percentages, not fractions.

tables.name: S24_Delirium_metapaths
tables.title: Metapaths connecting premature menopause, subacute delirium and dementia
tables.scope: DWPC comparisons for the three disease pairs.
notes: DWPC, degree-weighted path count, uses matrix walk products with damping −0.4. A metapath specifies ordered node and relationship types. Counts can include walks that revisit nodes.
The premature-menopause–delirium results comprise seven active schemas with DWPC printed to six decimal places; the complete inactive-schema output is unavailable.

blocks.title: Premature menopause and subacute delirium to dementia

tables.name: S25_Delirium_gene_sets
tables.title: Intermediate-gene sets linking premature menopause, delirium and dementia
tables.scope: Gene memberships and gene-level null comparisons, with extraction scopes distinguished.
notes: Gene identifiers are SPOKE identifiers and are stored as text. Blank values indicate missing or inapplicable data and are not zeros.

The 36 subacute-delirium–dementia genes use 11 fixed schemas and up to 50 paths per schema. Real and null extraction use identical deterministic ordering with no expansion cap. Empirical P values use 1,500 predicate-compatible pairs and a plus-one correction, followed by BH across 36 genes. This null is not degree-matched.

The second block uses the top five schemas and up to 200 paths per schema: 68 premature-menopause–delirium genes and 37 premature-menopause–dementia genes. The latter is a subset of Q1’s 55-gene set. Nineteen of the 68 delirium genes overlap Q1; 35 of the 36 delirium–dementia genes overlap Q1.
PM, premature menopause. The top-five set uses the five highest-DWPC schemas; it is distinct from the full Q1 55-gene set.

tables.name: S26_Delirium_null
tables.title: Random disease pairs and gene yields for the delirium–dementia comparison
tables.scope: The 1,500 predicate-compatible disease pairs used in the matched extraction comparison.
notes: Pairs were sampled with replacement using random seed 42 from diseases compatible with the first and last predicates; all 1,500 realized pairs were distinct. Observed endpoints are subacute delirium and dementia. The null uses the 11 observed schemas and identical ordered gene enumeration capped at 50 paths per schema.
The observed yield is 36 genes. The null mean is 3.6326667; 41 of 1,500 random yields are at least 36, giving plus-one empirical P = 42/1,501 = 0.0279813. Disease-node degree is not matched.

tables.name: S27_Delirium_enrichment
tables.title: Enrichment of premature-menopause–delirium and shared delirium–dementia genes
tables.scope: Separate enrichment analyses of 68 premature-menopause–delirium genes and 35 genes shared by Q1 and delirium–dementia.
notes: Adjusted P values are the Enrichr within-library multiple-testing results. BH denotes the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. Overlap is the number of input genes annotated to a term; term size is the number of genes annotated to that term in the library. Gene symbols are separated by semicolons.

The 68-gene analysis retains 174 significant term records from the union of two runs; library names are supplied per row. The 35-gene analysis contains all 1,370 returned GO Biological Process 2023 terms. The two input sets must not be pooled.

tables.name: S28_Cancer_connectivity
tables.title: Cancer-disease connectivity of selected compounds and random-compound background
tables.scope: Compound Cancer Gene Proximity Scores (CGPS) and all 1,000 random background scores.
notes: CGPS counts distinct cancer diseases reached through Compound–BINDS_CbP–Protein–ENCODES_GeP–Gene–Disease, using 1,884 cancer disease nodes. Binding and encoding retain direction; qualifying gene–disease relationships are traversed in either direction.

The background contains 1,000 compounds with at least one binding edge; 868 have nonzero scores. Both background percentile definitions are reported. Random compound identities and the sampling seed are unavailable. CGPS describes graph connectivity and does not estimate clinical cancer risk.
tables.question: Q7

tables.name: S29_Compound_targets
tables.title: Protein targets and encoding genes for the cancer-connectivity analysis
tables.scope: Complete target records for fezolinetant, elinzanetant, tamoxifen, letrozole and goserelin.
notes: Gene identifiers are SPOKE identifiers and are stored as text. Blank values indicate missing or inapplicable data and are not zeros.

Targets follow directed compound-to-protein BINDS_CbP relationships and gene-to-protein ENCODES_GeP relationships. Multiple proteins per gene are retained. Tamoxifen has 70 target genes. Diethylstilbestrol is included in the score table but was not included in this target-query run.
tables.question: Q7

tables.name: S30_Target_cancer_links
tables.title: Target-gene associations contributing to compound cancer-connectivity scores
tables.scope: Gene–disease relationships for the five compounds with complete target queries.
notes: Gene identifiers are SPOKE identifiers and are stored as text. Blank values indicate missing or inapplicable data and are not zeros.

Blank disease fields identify a target gene with no qualifying cancer-disease association. Disease counts overlap across target genes; CGPS is the number of distinct diseases per compound, not the sum of per-gene counts.

tables.name: S31_Neurokinin_networks
tables.title: Nodes and relationships in neurokinin-antagonist mechanistic networks
tables.scope: Dementia-related and breast-cancer-pathway neighborhoods of fezolinetant and elinzanetant.
notes: Relationship types are the recorded SPOKE predicates. Network labels identify separately exported neighborhoods; shared records across exports are retained. Direction fields follow the graph relationships and do not establish causal effects.
These are selected mechanistic neighborhoods, separate from the CGPS disease-count query. The breast-cancer network includes pathway WP4262.
tables.question: Q7

tables.name: S32_Drug_dementia_PageRank
tables.title: Dementia-seeded PageRank of selected breast-cancer therapies
tables.scope: Compound ranks and the distribution used to display the full compound background.
notes: Personalized PageRank measures graph proximity to the specified seed. Ranks and percentiles are descriptive. Membership in a ranked gene set does not require a direct gene–disease association.

Dementia seed DOID:1307; damping 0.85, maximum 500 iterations and tolerance 1e-20. The full ranking contains 2,432,054 compounds; the 50-bin histogram is a summarized display rather than a complete compound-level ranking.
tables.question: Q8

tables.name: S33_Drug_gene_membership
tables.title: Gene memberships shared by tamoxifen, letrozole and goserelin dementia routes
tables.scope: Gene memberships from identical three-edge queries and the seven disjoint overlap regions.
notes: Gene identifiers are SPOKE identifiers and are stored as text. Blank values indicate missing or inapplicable data and are not zeros.

The three sets contain 927, 174 and 237 genes, respectively. Genes are deduplicated over both intermediate positions. A TRUE/FALSE combination in the overlap summary defines a disjoint region. Eighty-one genes occur in all three sets.

Exclusive means absent from both other drug sets: tamoxifen has 599 exclusive genes, letrozole has two (PEG10 and TFPI2), and goserelin has none. Leuprolide returned no routes under this schema; this does not rule out other routes.
tables.question: Q8

tables.name: S34_Drug_dementia_routes
tables.title: Typed three-edge routes from breast-cancer therapies to dementia
tables.scope: All 19,734 returned route records for tamoxifen, letrozole and goserelin.
notes: Schema: Compound–[DOWNREGULATES_CdG or UPREGULATES_CuG]–Gene–[DOWNREGULATES_GPdG/KGdG or UPREGULATES_KGuG/GPuG]–Gene–ASSOCIATES_DaG–Dementia (DOID:1307). Traversal is undirected, with no result limit.

The identical queries returned 16,744 tamoxifen, 1,138 letrozole and 1,852 goserelin records. Parallel relationship records are retained. These Neo4j routes are separate from the DWPC graph calculations.
tables.question: Q8

tables.name: S35_Drug_gene_GO
tables.title: Biological-process enrichment of drug–dementia intermediate and exclusive gene sets
tables.scope: All 12,222 returned terms, with input sizes and annotation coverage for each gene set.
notes: Adjusted P values are the Enrichr within-library multiple-testing results. BH denotes the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. Overlap is the number of input genes annotated to a term; term size is the number of genes annotated to that term in the library. Gene symbols are separated by semicolons.

GO Biological Process 2023 with the default Enrichr background. Adjustment is separate for each gene-set analysis. Interpretation uses adjusted P < 0.05 and at least two overlapping genes; all returned terms are retained.

Exclusive sets exclude both other drugs. The two letrozole-exclusive genes yield only single-gene term overlaps; no term meets the two-gene reporting threshold. Goserelin has no exclusive genes, so no exclusive-set enrichment was run. Differences in enrichment P values are not between-drug tests.

tables.name: S37_Hormone_metapaths
tables.title: Estradiol and estrone connectivity to dementia-related diseases
tables.scope: Compound–target metapaths and cumulative DWPC by route category.
notes: DWPC, degree-weighted path count, uses matrix walk products with damping −0.4. A metapath specifies ordered node and relationship types. Counts can include walks that revisit nodes.

Estrone is one component of conjugated estrogens. Its identifier represents estrone and must not be interpreted as a query of the complete mixture. Source labels have been standardized to the compound actually queried.

All 3,006 compound–target–schema records have maximum length three. Route categories follow the analysis classification rule; “Other” includes schemas outside the named categories. Connectivity alone does not establish a treatment effect.
